newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni says GDR limit raised.
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni says GDR limit raised.

text.p: Komercni Banka a.s., the Czech Republic's largest commercial bank, has received permission from the central bank to increase the maximum amount of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) it may issue, bank spokeswoman Irena Satavova told Reuters on Friday.
Satavova said the limit had been raised to 13 percent of the bank's equity from a previous limit of 10 percent.
Central bank officials were not immediately available for comment.

After receiving central bank permission last year, Komercni initially converted 3.2 percent of its shares into GDRs for foreign investors, and has gradually increased the amount through subsequent conversions.
Satavova added that Komercni has used up the 10 percent limit, but she did not say when this had occurred.
Komercni GDRs, which are held by the Bank of New York, were trading on the London Stock Exchange on Friday at the equivalent of 1,943 crowns.
The Komercni GDRs have no voting rights, and the issue of the securities has not raised the bank's basic capital.

A Komercni official was quoted in the local media in February as saying that if the limit were raised, shares would come from the open market and not the state's holdings in the bank. The state still holds 48.7 percent in Komercni.
